# useAIChat

React hook for AI Gateway chat on top of `createAIGatewayClient`, with optional local tool support.

## Signature

```typescript
const useAIChat: (config: {
  client: AIGatewayClient;
  model: string;
  tools?: Record<string, AILocalTool>;
}) => {
  messages: AIChatMessage[];
  toolCalls: { id: string; name: string }[];
  status: "ready" | "submitted" | "streaming" | "error";
  error?: Error;
  sendMessage: (message: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  stop: () => void;
};
```

## Return Value

### `messages`

```typescript
interface AIChatMessage {
  id: string;
  role: "user" | "assistant";
  content: string;
}
```

### `toolCalls`

- **Type:** `{ id: string; name: string }[]`
- **Description:** Tool calls requested by the model in the active flow, including earlier tool rounds of the current request. This transient list is cleared when the response finishes, is stopped, or fails; it is never added to `messages` or conversation history.

Calls become available before local tool execution. They record requested tool names, not successful execution. Arguments and results remain internal.

### `status`

- **Type:** `"ready" | "submitted" | "streaming" | "error"`
- **Description:** Current request state. `submitted` covers waiting for the first text, local tool execution, and waiting for the model's next reply after a tool result. `streaming` begins when text arrives. `AIChat.Conversation` automatically shows a waiting indicator while `submitted`.

### `error`

- **Type:** `Error | undefined`
- **Description:** Last request error, if any

### `sendMessage()`

- **Type:** `(message: string) => Promise<boolean>`
- **Description:** Appends a user message and streams the assistant response
- **Returns:** `true` when the request completes successfully, `false` when the call is ignored, stopped, or fails

### `stop()`

- **Type:** `() => void`
- **Description:** Aborts the current request if one is in progress

### `tools`

Register local tools under a single object using `defineAIChatTool(...)`. Their schemas must implement both [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev/) validation and Standard JSON Schema generation (for example, Zod 4). Provider-native tools are not supported.

## Local tool API

`defineAIChatTool({ schema, execute, description? })` returns an `AILocalTool` with `kind: "local"`. The helper infers the first `execute` argument from the schema's **validated output**, including schema transformations. It does not execute or validate inputs when the tool is defined: `useAIChat` validates the model's arguments before calling `execute`.

`AIChatToolSchema<Input, Output>` is the schema contract: it combines Standard Schema validation with Standard JSON Schema generation. Zod 4 implements both. AppShell sends the schema's input JSON Schema to the AI Gateway; the executor receives the validated output.

The second `execute` argument is an `AIChatToolContext`:

| Property   | Type              | Description                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal`   | `AbortSignal`     | Cancellation signal for the active chat request. Forward it to `fetch` or other operations that support it. |
| `messages` | `AIChatMessage[]` | User/assistant text available to the current turn, excluding internal tool-call and tool-result messages.   |

Calling `stop()` or unmounting aborts the signal. Custom tool work must cooperate with cancellation; aborting does not undo side effects that have already happened. The authenticated AI Gateway example below forwards the signal to its request and checks the response status before returning a tool result.

## Working example: local tool execution

Click **Look up product** to run a real local tool through `useAIChat`: the scripted client requests `lookupProduct`, the hook validates its arguments, the tool reads a local inventory fixture, and the next scripted reply includes the internal tool result. The brief delay lets you see the requested tool name and try **Stop** before the lookup returns.

**Try invalid arguments** requests a number where the schema expects a string. Validation prevents tool execution and returns a tool-result error to the scripted client; this is not a top-level chat `error`.

The preview needs no authentication, backend, or model. It imports `useState` from `react`, and `Button`, `Text`, `defineAIChatTool`, `useAIChat`, `AIChatToolSchema`, and `AIGatewayClient` from `@tailor-platform/app-shell` (the last two are types). Its small dependency-free schema implements the Standard Schema contracts directly; an application can use a schema library such as Zod 4, as shown below.

<example-preview name="local-tool-execution"></example-preview>

```tsx
function LocalToolExecution() {
  const [config] = useState(() => {
    const jsonSchema = {
      type: "object",
      properties: { sku: { type: "string", minLength: 1 } },
      required: ["sku"],
    };
    const schema: AIChatToolSchema<{ sku: string }> = {
      "~standard": {
        version: 1,
        vendor: "documentation-demo",
        validate(value) {
          if (
            typeof value === "object" &&
            value !== null &&
            "sku" in value &&
            typeof value.sku === "string" &&
            value.sku.length > 0
          ) {
            return { value: { sku: value.sku } };
          }
          return { issues: [{ message: "sku must be a non-empty string." }] };
        },
        jsonSchema: {
          input: () => jsonSchema,
          output: () => jsonSchema,
        },
      },
    };
    const lookupProduct = defineAIChatTool({
      description: "Look up a product in the local demo inventory",
      schema,
      async execute({ sku }, { signal }) {
        // Keep the tool active briefly so its requested name and Stop can be tried.
        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800));
        signal.throwIfAborted();
        const products = [{ sku: "NOTE-1", name: "Notebook", available: 12 }];
        return products.find((product) => product.sku === sku) ?? { sku, error: "Not found" };
      },
    });
    const client: AIGatewayClient = {
      async *streamChatCompletion({ messages, signal }) {
        signal?.throwIfAborted();
        const lastMessage = messages.at(-1);
        if (lastMessage?.role === "user") {
          yield {
            type: "tool-call",
            toolCallId: crypto.randomUUID(),
            toolName: "lookupProduct",
            argumentsText: JSON.stringify({
              sku: lastMessage.content === "Try invalid arguments" ? 42 : "NOTE-1",
            }),
          };
          yield { type: "done", finishReason: "tool_calls" };
          return;
        }
        if (lastMessage?.role === "tool") {
          yield { type: "text-delta", text: `Local tool result: ${lastMessage.content}` };
        }
        yield { type: "done", finishReason: "stop" };
      },
    };
    return { client, model: "scripted-demo", tools: { lookupProduct } };
  });
  const { messages, toolCalls, status, error, sendMessage, stop } = useAIChat(config);
  const busy = status === "submitted" || status === "streaming";

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <Text.p>
        Replies are scripted locally, but useAIChat validates and executes the real local tool. No
        prompt is sent to a server or model.
      </Text.p>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button type="button" disabled={busy} onClick={() => void sendMessage("Look up NOTE-1")}>
          Look up product
        </Button>
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          disabled={busy}
          onClick={() => void sendMessage("Try invalid arguments")}
        >
          Try invalid arguments
        </Button>
        <Button type="button" variant="outline" disabled={!busy} onClick={stop}>
          Stop
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Text.p role="status">Status: {status}</Text.p>
      <Text.p>Requested tools: {toolCalls.map((call) => call.name).join(", ") || "None"}</Text.p>
      <div role="log" aria-label="Local tool conversation" className="flex flex-col gap-2">
        {messages.length === 0 && <Text.p>Run a lookup to start the conversation.</Text.p>}
        {messages.map((message) => (
          <Text.p key={message.id}>
            <strong>{message.role}:</strong> {message.content}
          </Text.p>
        ))}
      </div>
      {error && <Text.p role="alert">{error.message}</Text.p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage with an authenticated AI Gateway

Unlike the scripted preview, this setup calls a real AI Gateway and an application-owned API. Create the clients once outside rendering and supply your own endpoints and authentication configuration.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  createAuthClient,
  createAIGatewayClient,
  defineAIChatTool,
  useAIChat,
} from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";
import { z } from "zod/v4";

const authClient = createAuthClient({
  clientId: "your-client-id",
  appUri: "https://xyz.erp.dev",
});

const aiClient = createAIGatewayClient({
  gatewayUri: "https://your-ai-gateway.example.com",
  authClient,
});

const lookupCustomer = defineAIChatTool({
  description: "Look up a customer in the current workspace",
  schema: z.object({
    customerId: z.string(),
  }),
  async execute({ customerId }, { signal }) {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/customers/${encodeURIComponent(customerId)}`, { signal });
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Customer lookup failed: ${response.status}`);
    }
    return response.json();
  },
});

export function ChatScreen() {
  const { messages, toolCalls, sendMessage, status, stop, error } = useAIChat({
    client: aiClient,
    model: "gpt-5-mini",
    tools: {
      lookupCustomer,
    },
  });

  return (
    <div>
      {messages.map((message) => (
        <div key={message.id}>
          {message.role}: {message.content}
        </div>
      ))}
      {toolCalls.map((call) => (
        <div key={call.id}>Tool call: {call.name}</div>
      ))}

      <Button
        onClick={() => void sendMessage("Hello")}
        disabled={status === "submitted" || status === "streaming"}
      >
        Send
      </Button>
      <Button onClick={stop} disabled={status !== "submitted" && status !== "streaming"}>
        Stop
      </Button>
      {error ? <div>{error.message}</div> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Notes

- AppShell chooses the appropriate AI Gateway transport automatically
- Public messages stay user/assistant text-first; tool calls and results never become conversation messages
- System prompts and custom history shaping should use the low-level client directly
- `stop()` keeps already-streamed assistant text, clears the active `toolCalls`, and ignores late events from the stopped request
